broad.text: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

problem_constrained.text: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy forms several primary non-eutectic phases during solidification and exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence. Under rapid cooling, slower cooling, and subsequent reheating assessed by thermal analysis, what single intervention could increase amorphous retention and thermal stability while overcoming extensive primary crystallization? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the alloy’s reported glass formation and crystallization behavior, the relevant cooling-rate and reheating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

expert_context.text: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy previously showed limited amorphous retention and a complicated thermal response. Earlier thermal studies of Ni–P and Pd–Ni–P alloys found that rapid quenching could produce amorphous material, but that its stability was limited during subsequent heating. The design challenge is therefore to obtain robust glass formation across relevant cooling conditions without sacrificing stability during reheating. What single intervention could improve amorphous retention and thermal stability during solidification and thermal analysis? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the reported behavior of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20, the cooling-rate and reheating conditions under which it should or should not succeed, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that would falsify it.

hidden_target.material_initial_state: Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 alloy prepared from ≥99.9 wt.% elemental powders by arc melting and remelted at least six times; examined both as a slower-cooled arc-melted ingot and as ~20 μm melt-spun ribbon.
hidden_target.intervention: The study adjusted the Fe/Co/Mn ratios and reduced P to 15 at.% relative to the previously studied Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 composition, then compared arc solidification with rapid melt spinning on a copper wheel at 40 m/s.
hidden_target.conditions: Arc melting was performed under 99.999% Ar in a water-cooled copper crucible. Ingot cooling began near 1459 K and averaged 95.9 K/s (maximum 215.2 K/s before and 85.9 K/s after eutectic crystallization). DSC heating/cooling used Ar and 20 K/min. Ribbons were rapidly quenched to ~20 μm thickness and subsequently heated by DSC at 20 K/min.
hidden_target.structural_mediator: A eutectic-dominated solidification structure comprising fine, predominantly rod-like eutectic colonies; under slower cooling, inter-colony partitioning produces an Fe–Ni–Mn-rich solid solution and P/Cr-rich phosphides, whereas rapid quenching retains a fully amorphous ribbon.
hidden_target.mechanism: Increasing Fe and Co, reducing Mn, and lowering P from 20 to 15 at.% decreases primary solid-solution crystallization and limits high-temperature phosphide formation, shifting solidification toward cooperative eutectic growth. Rapid cooling suppresses elemental segregation and phosphide nucleation, preserving amorphous order; slower cooling permits P-driven partitioning and formation of multiple transition-metal phosphides. On reheating, the amorphous ribbon devitrifies through sequential TM-rich ordering, possible early phosphide formation, and final formation of a TM solid solution plus P-rich phosphides.
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: Relative to the prior Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy, the modified alloy should exhibit a simpler, predominantly eutectic transformation sequence and a larger eutectic fraction; relative to slower-cooled ingots and simpler TM–P glasses, rapid melt spinning should yield a fully amorphous state with a broad, comparatively thermally stable crystallization interval.
hidden_target.baseline: Primary comparison: previously studied Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20, which showed multiple solidification arrests from eutectic, primary, and non-eutectic crystallization. Processing comparison: the slower-cooled arc-melted ingot. Thermal-stability comparisons were simpler Ni–P, Pd–Ni–P, Fe–Ni–P–C, and related TM–P systems.
hidden_target.boundary: Complete amorphization was demonstrated for ~20 μm ribbons melt-spun at 40 m/s, not for bulk samples. Slower/near-equilibrium cooling produced a multiphase crystalline ingot. The reported thermal stability applies to DSC heating at 20 K/min; no glass transition was detected, so γ could not be evaluated. Mechanical properties were not tested.
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: Infrared temperature–time thermography and DSC tested whether solidification was eutectic-dominated; XRD distinguished the amorphous ribbon from the multiphase ingot; SEM/BSE with EDS mapping tested eutectic morphology and elemental partitioning. Ribbon DSC measured the devitrification sequence and crystallization span.
hidden_target.actual_result: Thermography showed cooling from 1459 K to an approximately 1007 K arrest within 2.1 s, followed by a ~2 s eutectic plateau and visible contraction/flattening. Bulk DSC showed a dominant eutectic exotherm at 1281.9–1256.4 K with −170.7 J/g, versus main melting over 1235.5–1347.3 K with 180.4 J/g. The ribbon was fully amorphous by XRD and crystallized in three stages beginning at 659 K, with events near 699 K and 735–773 K, completion near 820 K, total enthalpy 180.4 J/g, and ΔTc ≈161 K. The ingot contained Fe–Ni (Fm-3m), CrCoP (Pnma), Ni3P (I-4), and MnNiP (P-62m) phases. Thus, the compositional modification simplified solidification and increased eutectic dominance, while rapid cooling suppressed segregation and phosphide formation sufficiently to produce an amorphous ribbon.
